The supplied parent is already close to the record, so a purely local continuation of the same heuristic is likely to stagnate. The new design attacks three independent bottlenecks instead of only polishing the parent:

A. Exact finite-sum feasibility is built into a large part of the search by using an anti-palindromic half-vector representation. For an even length `n = 2m`, any `x in [0,1]^m` yields a feasible full vector `h` of length `n` by setting the first half to `x` and the second half to the reversed complement of `x`. This satisfies `0 <= h <= 1` and `sum(h) = n/2` structurally, with no separate reopenable projection that silently changes the evaluated objective.

B. The main continuous optimizer is no longer only a fixed set of ad-hoc gradient line searches. A smooth-max mixed finite-difference/BFGS search in the anti-palindromic subspace is combined with an exact-sum one-dimensional minimax line search in full-dimensional spaces. The smoothed objective only guides the search; every stored candidate is accepted or rejected by re-evaluating the exact task objective `max(np.correlate(h, 1-h, mode="full")) * (2/n)`.

C. Multiple resolutions are searched deliberately. The discrete objective includes the finite-support boundary terms and scaling by `2/n`, so the optimum ratio can depend on `n`. Therefore the program repeatedly tries sibling lengths around the parent, as well as shorter balanced sequences that may exploit rounding effects and are explicitly preferred when no worse. Parent correctness and objective consistency are retained by always evaluating the returned vector with the task metric.

Small optional anti-palindromic mixed-integer searches are also included for relatively coarse lengths. They are only seeds and exact-candidate producers; the program does not claim global optimality because the full non-integer problem is nonconvex and the integer relaxation is time limited. If those MILP attempts fail, the algorithm continues using continuous/smooth/stochastic local-global mechanisms and returns the exact parent fallback.
